Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this on. We're gearing up to onboard Redwood into our private VPC (prod-rw-01) and need clarity on how logs, metrics and traces will be exported to our Splunk Cloud/SIEM.

Samir —

Thanks for the detail. Proposed architecture (short):
1) Runtime emits structured JSON logs to a local forwarder (sidecar or host). We recommend host-forwarder when you run many small runtime pods on the same host to reduce duplicated TLS connections.
2) Forwarder runs an OpenTelemetry Collector instance in push mode to Splunk HEC using mTLS. We will accept HEC over TLS and OTLP over TLS depending on your preference.
3) For traces, inject the OTEL exporter into our runtime process (we provide a lightweight shim) which sends to the local OTEL collector. Sampling is controlled by the collector with dynamic sampling rules exposed via our control plane (no cleartext user ids in spans).

Example trace hook (pseudo):
- register_span_processor("redwood-collector", attributes={"rw.app": getenv("APP_NAME")})
- redact_and_hash("user_id") => replace with sha256 digest hex

Network/Egress checklist (high level):
- Allow egress from host-forwarder/collector IPs to splunkcloud.finbank.svc:8088 (TLS)
- Allow AWS VPC endpoints if using a transit VPC; otherwise we can peer during on-prem staging
- Port 443 for control-plane callbacks (mutual auth) if you enable remote rollout controls

I'll attach a runnable OTEL collector fragment for your team to test. We'll also add an RBAC step to ensure only hashes are emitted for user-level identifiers.

Marcus Lin
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
